record.what_it_does: Netlify is a platform for building, deploying, and hosting web apps, and its REST API lets developers manage atomic deploys, sites, forms, DNS, environment variables, and more programmatically.
record.auth_notes: Personal Access Tokens (PATs) are static bearer tokens generated in user settings, intended for personal/manual scripting use. Netlify explicitly requires OAuth2 for any public/third-party integration: 'If you're making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.' OAuth apps are registered in Netlify user settings and use the authorize endpoint at https://app.netlify.com/authorize.
record.access_notes: Any developer can sign up for a free Netlify account and immediately generate a Personal Access Token from Applications > Personal access tokens, or register an OAuth application in user settings, with no approval or payment required to obtain working API credentials.

evidence.quote: If you're making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.
To authenticate API requests, include the token in the authorization header: Authorization: Bearer
Use your PAT for manual authentication in shell scripts or commands that use the Netlify API
This is a REST-style API that uses JSON for serialization and OAuth 2 for authentication.
Send deploy notifications to email, a pull/merge request, or an external web service
